name: Theme Contrast & Button State Visibility Audit
note: The contrast comparison in this gate had never executed. It was guarded by `dist > 30 || backgroundImage.includes(gradient)`, and the button it measures is always a gradient, so white text on a white background passed. 2026-09-30: the threshold is now the WCAG contrast ratio (3:1), not RGB distance (external audit V06).

mutations.name: the selected language button is given text the same colour as its background
mutations.why: Text at #4a8bf5 sits 17 units from the gradient stop #3b82f6, under the threshold of 30 — the selected language is then unreadable against its own button. The first attempt used #dbeafe, which is 191 units away and correctly passed: an unfair mutation reported as a gate defect until the numbers were checked. Under the ratio rule: #4a8bf5 on #3b82f6 is 1.1:1.

mutations.name: the selected language gets pale blue text — far in RGB, unreadable to the eye
mutations.why: External audit V06: #93c5fd sits 110 units from #3b82f6, so the old distance rule (>30) passed it. Its contrast is 2.0:1. This is the case the distance rule could not see.

mutations.name: the stats tab goes back to white on light amber
mutations.why: White on #f59e0b is 2.15:1 — measured when the stats tab joined this gate on 2026-09-30, and darkened then.

mutations.name: a dark-theme rule goes back to the class nothing sets
mutations.why: D24: four dark-theme rules were written for body.dark-theme; the theme manager sets theme-<id>, so none applied.

mutations.name: the opponent count keeps the light theme colour on the dark theme
mutations.why: D24: #9333ea on the dark card reads under 3:1 — what players saw until 2026-10-21.

mutations.name: the battle gauge track goes back to a black wash
mutations.why: D24: rgba(0,0,0,.08) on a dark card is darker than the card — the track does not show.

mutations.name: the hint button takes the dark amber
mutations.why: D24: measured before choosing — the dark amber read 4.23:1 and stood 2.14:1 off the dark surface; the yellow 6.58 and 11.1.
